name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Main's runs go one at a time, so two merges close together never pick the
# same next version. A pull request's older run is cancelled by its newer one.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test --locked

  chart:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
      - name: helm lint
        run: |
          helm lint chart/releaseway --strict \
            --set bucket.endpoint=https://account.r2.cloudflarestorage.com --set bucket.name=cache \
            --set secrets.token=token \
            --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.host=cache.example.com --set ingress.tls.enabled=true
          helm lint chart/releaseway --strict \
            --set existingSecret=releaseway --set 'hosts={github.com,example.com}' --set maxBytes=1000

  # Every merge to main is a patch release: the latest vX.Y.Z tag with Z one
  # higher. A minor or major bump is still a tag pushed by hand, and the
  # merges after it count on from there. A commit that already has a v tag
  # (pushed by hand) gets no second one.
  version:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: [test, chart]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.next.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - id: next
        run: |
          if git tag --points-at HEAD | grep -q '^v'; then
            echo "$GITHUB_SHA is already tagged; nothing to release."
            exit 0
          fi
          tags=$(git tag -l 'v*' | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' || true)
          latest=$(echo "$tags" | sort -V | tail -n 1)
          if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
            next=v0.0.1
          else
            IFS=. read -r major minor patch <<< "${latest#v}"
            next="v$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          fi
          echo "latest $latest, next $next"
          echo "tag=$next" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  image:
    needs: [test, chart, version]
    # `version` is skipped on pull requests and tags; that is no reason to
    # skip this.
    if: ${{ !failure() && !cancelled() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          tags: |
            type=ref,event=branch
            type=ref,event=pr
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }},enable=${{ needs.version.outputs.tag != '' }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          # amd64 alone: arm64 would be built under QEMU, at many times the
          # time, for a machine nothing here runs on. Adding it is adding it
          # here and setup-qemu-action before buildx.
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          build-args: VERSION=${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

  # On a vX.Y.Z tag pushed by hand, or on a merge to main with the tag
  # `version` picked, publish the chart to oci://ghcr.io/<owner>/charts/releaseway
  # with its version and appVersion set from the tag. A merge's tag, and its
  # GitHub release with notes of what went in, are made here, after its image
  # is pushed, so a release never names an image that is not there. A tag made
  # with this workflow's token starts no workflow, which is why this does not
  # wait for the tag's own run.
  chart-release:
    needs: [image, version]
    if: >-
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') || needs.version.outputs.tag != '')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      packages: write
    env:
      TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Release the merge
        if: needs.version.outputs.tag != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: gh release create "$TAG" --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
      - run: |
          version="${TAG#v}"
          helm package chart/releaseway --version "$version" --app-version "$version"
          echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | helm registry login ghcr.io -u "${{ github.actor }}" --password-stdin
          helm push "releaseway-$version.tgz" "oci://ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/charts"

content.content:
1	# releaseway
2	
3	A pull-through cache of release and archive downloads in an S3 bucket (R2,
4	S3, or anything that speaks S3's API). `GET /<host>/<path>` answers with
5	`https://<host>/<path>`: from the bucket when it has it, and otherwise
6	fetched once, stored, and answered from there.
7	
8	By default it caches GitHub's download hosts: `github.com`,
9	`codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com` and
10	`release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, which is where a repository's
11	archives and release assets come from. It was made for Bazel, whose
12	rulesets and toolchains are mostly GitHub archives: pointed at releaseway,
13	a build keeps working while GitHub is down, after a tag's archive has gone,
14	or on a machine that cannot reach GitHub at all.
15	
16	- **Only the configured hosts**, and only paths that could name a file
17	  there: no query, no empty, `.` or `..` segments. Anything else is a 404,
18	  and a redirect to another host is refused.
19	- **Only fetched with the token.** A file the bucket has not got yet is
20	  fetched only for a caller with the token, as a bearer token or as the
21	  password of Basic auth, which is what `~/.netrc` gives Bazel, curl and
22	  most other tools. Without it the answer is 401, so nobody else can fill
23	  the bucket, or have it hold something of theirs under your name. What is
24	  cached already is anybody's, as it is upstream.
25	- **Never fetched again.** Tools that name a download by its hash (Bazel's
26	  `sha256`, a lockfile's integrity) fail a file that changed upstream
27	  whichever copy it came from, so the first copy is the one to keep.
28	- **One file at a time through a scratch folder**, never whole in memory,
29	  up to 2 GiB each by default.
30	- **Up without a bucket**, answering 503 and saying why in its log, so a
31	  deploy made before its Secret still rolls out.
32	
33	## Using it with Bazel
34	
35	A downloader config, passed with `--experimental_downloader_config`, that
36	tries releaseway first and GitHub second. When two rewrites match one URL,
37	Bazel tries both, in order, so a cache that is down costs one failed
38	request:
39	
40	```
41	rewrite (github\.com|codeload\.github\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|release-assets\.githubusercontent\.com)/(.*) cache.example.com/$1/$2
42	rewrite (github\.com|codeload\.github\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|release-assets\.githubusercontent\.com)/(.*) $1/$2
43	```
44	
45	and, on a machine that may add to the cache, `~/.netrc` (Bazel reads it for
46	rewritten URLs too):
47	
48	```
49	machine cache.example.com
50	login bazel
51	password <the token>
52	```
53	
54	## Configuration
55	
56	| Variable | |
57	| --- | --- |
58	| `RELEASEWAY_BUCKET_ENDPOINT` | e.g. `https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` |
59	| `RELEASEWAY_BUCKET` | the bucket's name |
60	| `RELEASEWAY_BUCKET_REGION` | `auto` (R2's) unless set |
61	| `RELEASEWAY_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `RELEASEWAY_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | a key that can read and write the bucket |
62	| `RELEASEWAY_TOKEN` | what a caller must send for anything to be fetched; without it, only what is cached is served |
63	| `RELEASEWAY_HOSTS` | the hosts cached, comma-separated; GitHub's four unless set |
64	| `RELEASEWAY_MAX_BYTES` | the largest file fetched; 2 GiB unless set |
65	| `RELEASEWAY_SCRATCH` | where a download waits on its way to the bucket; `/tmp` unless set |
66	| `LISTEN_ADDR` | `0.0.0.0:8080` unless set |
67	
68	It logs JSON lines on stdout, one per request, and stops on SIGTERM.
69	`GET /healthz` is for a readiness probe.
70	
71	## Kubernetes
72	
73	The chart is published to `oci://ghcr.io/u9g/charts/releaseway` with every
74	release, and its image to `ghcr.io/u9g/releaseway`:
75	
76	```sh
77	kubectl create secret generic releaseway \
78	  --from-literal=ACCESS_KEY_ID=... --from-literal=SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... \
79	  --from-literal=TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
80	helm install releaseway oci://ghcr.io/u9g/charts/releaseway --version <version> \
81	  --set bucket.endpoint=https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com \
82	  --set bucket.name=<bucket> --set existingSecret=releaseway
83	```
84	
85	`chart/releaseway/values.yaml` has the rest: the hosts, an Ingress, the
86	scratch volume's size, resources. Or `secrets.*` instead of
87	`existingSecret`, for a Secret the chart makes.
88	
89	## Developing
90	
91	```sh
92	cargo test    # a stand-in bucket and a stand-in GitHub, nothing over the network
93	cargo run     # with the variables above
94	```
95

# releaseway

A pull-through cache of release and archive downloads in an S3 bucket (R2,
S3, or anything that speaks S3's API). `GET /<host>/<path>` answers with
`https://<host>/<path>`: from the bucket when it has it, and otherwise
fetched once, stored, and answered from there.

By default it caches GitHub's download hosts: `github.com`,
`codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com` and
`release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, which is where a repository's
archives and release assets come from. It was made for Bazel, whose
rulesets and toolchains are mostly GitHub archives: pointed at releaseway,
a build keeps working while GitHub is down, after a tag's archive has gone,
or on a machine that cannot reach GitHub at all.

- **Only the configured hosts**, and only paths that could name a file
  there: no query, no empty, `.` or `..` segments. Anything else is a 404,
  and a redirect to another host is refused.
- **Only fetched with the token.** A file the bucket has not got yet is
  fetched only for a caller with the token, as a bearer token or as the
  password of Basic auth, which is what `~/.netrc` gives Bazel, curl and
  most other tools. Without it the answer is 401, so nobody else can fill
  the bucket, or have it hold something of theirs under your name. What is
  cached already is anybody's, as it is upstream.
- **Never fetched again.** Tools that name a download by its hash (Bazel's
  `sha256`, a lockfile's integrity) fail a file that changed upstream
  whichever copy it came from, so the first copy is the one to keep.
- **One file at a time through a scratch folder**, never whole in memory,
  up to 2 GiB each by default.
- **Up without a bucket**, answering 503 and saying why in its log, so a
  deploy made before its Secret still rolls out.

## Using it with Bazel

A downloader config, passed with `--experimental_downloader_config`, that
tries releaseway first and GitHub second. When two rewrites match one URL,
Bazel tries both, in order, so a cache that is down costs one failed
request:

```
rewrite (github\.com|codeload\.github\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|release-assets\.githubusercontent\.com)/(.*) cache.example.com/$1/$2
rewrite (github\.com|codeload\.github\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|release-assets\.githubusercontent\.com)/(.*) $1/$2
```

and, on a machine that may add to the cache, `~/.netrc` (Bazel reads it for
rewritten URLs too):

```
machine cache.example.com
login bazel
password <the token>
```

## Configuration

| Variable | |
| --- | --- |
| `RELEASEWAY_BUCKET_ENDPOINT` | e.g. `https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` |
| `RELEASEWAY_BUCKET` | the bucket's name |
| `RELEASEWAY_BUCKET_REGION` | `auto` (R2's) unless set |
| `RELEASEWAY_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `RELEASEWAY_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | a key that can read and write the bucket |
| `RELEASEWAY_TOKEN` | what a caller must send for anything to be fetched; without it, only what is cached is served |
| `RELEASEWAY_HOSTS` | the hosts cached, comma-separated; GitHub's four unless set |
| `RELEASEWAY_MAX_BYTES` | the largest file fetched; 2 GiB unless set |
| `RELEASEWAY_SCRATCH` | where a download waits on its way to the bucket; `/tmp` unless set |
| `LISTEN_ADDR` | `0.0.0.0:8080` unless set |

It logs JSON lines on stdout, one per request, and stops on SIGTERM.
`GET /healthz` is for a readiness probe.

## Kubernetes

The chart is published to `oci://ghcr.io/u9g/charts/releaseway` with every
release, and its image to `ghcr.io/u9g/releaseway`:

```sh
kubectl create secret generic releaseway \
  --from-literal=ACCESS_KEY_ID=... --from-literal=SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... \
  --from-literal=TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
helm install releaseway oci://ghcr.io/u9g/charts/releaseway --version <version> \
  --set bucket.endpoint=https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com \
  --set bucket.name=<bucket> --set existingSecret=releaseway
```

`chart/releaseway/values.yaml` has the rest: the hosts, an Ingress, the
scratch volume's size, resources. Or `secrets.*` instead of
`existingSecret`, for a Secret the chart makes.

## Developing

```sh
cargo test    # a stand-in bucket and a stand-in GitHub, nothing over the network
cargo run     # with the variables above
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs fmt, clippy and the tests, and lints
the chart. Every merge to main is a patch release: a `vX.Y.Z` tag, the
image, and the chart. A minor or major version is a tag
pushed by hand, and the merges after it count on from there. The image is
amd64 alone.

# Plan: deterministic replay fixtures for releaseway tests

## Context

The tests in `src/cache.rs` and `src/main.rs` stand in for GitHub and the bucket with hand-written routes: one fixed body ("the archive"), one redirect, and a catch-all 404. They prove the cache logic but not the shapes real upstream sends (redirect `Location` headers, ETags, content types, 404 bodies, large bodies). They also share one scratch directory (`releaseway-test-<pid>`) across parallel tests, so two tests that fetch at once can collide on `download-0`.

The goal is to record real upstream exchanges once, store them as fixtures in the repo, and have the tests replay them. A test then gets the same bytes and headers on every run, with no network, and fails loudly when a request has no recorded answer.

## Approach

1. **Fixture format.** One directory per scenario under `fixtures/` at the repo root (not under `src/`). Each has a `manifest.json` listing exchanges in order: `{ method, path, status, headers, body }`, where `body` names a file beside it. Bodies are stored as files so archives stay out of JSON, and each is named by its sha256 so the tests can check it, which fits the project's hash-based model.
2. **Replay stand-in.** Replace the catch-all 404 in `cache()` with a replayer that serves the next matching exchange by method and path. Any request with no match panics, so an unexpected upstream call fails the test instead of quietly returning 404. The bucket stand-in stays an in-memory map, seeded from a fixture when a scenario needs an object already cached.
3. **Redirects replayed as recorded.** Record the `Location` GitHub actually sends. The replayer rewrites hosts in it to `<origin>/<host>/<path>`, which is the form `Cache::new` already accepts via `origin`.
4. **Per-test scratch directory.** Give each test its own temp dir (e.g. include a counter or the test name) so parallel tests cannot share `download-N` files.
5. **Recording is manual.** An `#[ignore]` test that fetches from live GitHub with a token and writes the fixture directory. It is run by hand and never in CI, so CI stays offline and deterministic. Recording does not live in the binary, so there is no record mode in production code.

## Critical files

- `src/cache.rs`: test module (`named`, `same` tests stay as they are). Add an ignored `record` test only if it can reuse `Cache` without changing its public API.
- `src/main.rs`: test module. `cache()` helper switches to the replayer; the three existing tests keep their assertions and read the same fixtures.
- `fixtures/<scenario>/manifest.json` and body files: new, one scenario each for archive-by-redirect, upstream 404, and a cached object already in the bucket.

No changes to the production code paths (`serve`, `fetch`, `authorized`, `named`).

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, matching CI.
- `cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1` and the default parallel run both pass, with the same results on repeat runs.
- Negative check: temporarily delete one manifest exchange, confirm the test panics on the unmatched request, then restore it.
- Recording: run the ignored test once with a real token, confirm the regenerated fixtures replay green offline.

## Choices made without asking

- Interpreted "replay fixtures" as recorded HTTP exchanges replayed in tests, not a replay mode in the server.
- Recording is an ignored test run by hand, not part of CI.
- Fixtures live at repo-root `fixtures/`, not inside `src/`.
- Implementation goes on the designated branch `claude/replay-fixture-proposed_plan-aey35e`.
